job_application.reformulated_text:
A job applicant submits job applications to multiple companies. Each job application is associated with a company. A company confirms receipt of a job application and rates the application. 

A job application can transition to a job interview negotiation if a company wants to proceed with the applicant. 

A job interview negotiation can transition to a probation phase if the company wants the job applicant to work for them. 

During the probation phase, the job applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the job applicant. 

A job application can end in one of two ways: either the job becomes permanent, or the job applicant rates the company C or less. 

If the job becomes permanent, the process ends. 

If the job applicant rates the company C or less, they continue to receive job offers but no longer have to report job applications. 

Reviews for a company can only be seen by job applicants after 1 year.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text:
To support planning, taking, and extending a maternity leave, a process can be created with the following steps:

1. Fetch information about potential maternity leave models, including their duration in months and the split of leave between parents.
2. Present the parent with the available models to select from.
3. Collect relevant information from the parent, such as their leave preferences and company policies.
4. Notify the Social Security and the Company of the parent's intention to take maternity leave in a timely manner.
5. Gather information from the Company regarding their maternity leave policies and procedures.
6. At the end of the maternity leave period, allow the parent to decide whether to extend their leave.

The parent's selection of a maternity leave model persists throughout the process, and their decision to extend their leave at the end of the period is a distinct condition that causes a transition from the current leave period to a potential extended leave period.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
To gather information about work accidents and almost work accidents, a process is created that involves the following steps:

1. An insured individual experiences an accident or almost experiences an accident while performing their gainful employment, which includes working from home, on the direct route to or from work, or during training sessions that provide specific professional knowledge.

2. The accident or almost accident occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment, such as when taking a child to or collecting them from a childcare facility, or when using advocacy groups or professional associations.

3. For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, an accident is considered a work accident if it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to their school or university education, or if it occurs during a school event or school-related event.

4. In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner, providing accommodation for guests, secondary occupations for selling agricultural products, building work for the establishment, and neighbourhood assistance for another establishment.

5. Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident or donating blood, and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation.

6. The insured individual must inform their employer immediately of any work accident, any incident that would almost have led to an accident, any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover, and any defect discovered in protection systems.

7. The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services.

8. The responsible accident insurance provider must be notified of every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days, in full or in part, within five days.

9. As a self-employed person, accidents involving people you employ and those that involve you must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time.

10. Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate, and schools, educational facilities, and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate.

11. In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.

The process involves two main entities: the job application and the job applicant. A job application is created when the applicant submits an application to a company. The applicant is then required to report the company to which they submitted the application. 

Based on the job application, new potential job offers are sent to the applicant. The company to which the application was submitted must confirm receipt of the application and rate the application. The applicant and the company can negotiate a job interview. 

When a company wants the applicant to work for them, the applicant enters the probation phase. After the probation phase, the applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the applicant. 

Reviews for a company can only be seen by job applicants after 1 year. If a job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless the applicant previously rated the company C or less, in which case the applicant continues to receive job offers but no longer has to report. The text does not specify what happens to the job application after the probation phase, nor what happens to the applicant's obligation to report if they rated the company C or less.

The process involves several entities: the accident, the insured employment, the employer, the employee, the Labour Inspectorate, the accident insurance provider, and the competent directorate. 

A work accident is considered to be an accident that occurs in the following circumstances: 
- the accident occurs in a location, at a time and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment
- when working from home
- on the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work, to lunch or on the way home, whereby carpools are also protected
- for training sessions that serve to provide specific professional knowledge, whereby an accident on the way to or from the training centre is considered a work accident
- on the direct route from home, or from the workplace or training centre to a doctor and back, if this interrupts the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work or the route home (the doctor's visit must be notified to the employer in advance)
- on the way to or from the workplace or training centre with the purpose of taking a child to or collecting them from a childcare facility, a daycare facility, external care or a school, insofar as they have a supervisory responsibility for the child
- when making use of advocacy groups or professional associations (e.g. Chamber of Labour, trade union federation, guild etc.)

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren and students, an accident is considered to be a work accident if, amongst other things:
- the accident occurs in a location, at a time and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education or the compulsory kindergarten year that forms the basis of the insurance
- when taking part in a school event or school-related event
- on the direct route from the child's place of residence or permanent accommodation to kindergarten or a school visit or on the way home
- when performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum and/or the study regulations
- in certain professional (training) orientations

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner, providing accommodation for guests, secondary occupations for selling agricultural products, building work for the establishment, and neighbourhood assistance for another establishment.

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident or donating blood, and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation (fire brigade, water rescue, Red Cross, Alpine Rescue, air rescue, etc.).

The employee must inform the employer immediately of: any work accident, any incident that would almost have led to an accident, any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover, any defect discovered in protection systems. The employer must inform the Labour Inspectorate immediately of any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury, if it has not been reported to the emergency services.

The accident insurance provider must be informed of every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days, in full or in part, within five days. As a self-employed person, accidents involving people you employ and those that involve you must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time.

Students and schoolchildren must report accidents to the competent directorate. Schools, educational facilities and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate. In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.
